title: Occupancy and Residency Certification Rules on a Borrower's Death and Changes in the Household
content:
## Recording a death

Under the Occupancy and Residency Certification product, a borrower's death is recorded only from an accepted death notice submission carrying the death certificate the plan requires as death documentation. Any person whose profile type is listed in the plan's death-report channel may report it — the borrower, an eligible non-borrowing spouse, an ineligible non-borrowing spouse, a successor in interest or an authorized third party. A caller who is not yet a confirmed successor in interest is told, within the plan's successor-confirmation period in calendar days, which documents confirm that status.

A profile is reclassified or closed for a death only on an accepted death notice on file for that profile. The death notice on the company's submission records is the authority; a caller's report alone does not reclassify or close a profile.

## Reclassification when the loan continues

When a certifying borrower dies and the loan continues, the profile moves to the plan named for its current plan in the plan's reclassification setting:

| Plan held at the death | Moves to |
|---|---|
| Joint Borrower Certification, with a surviving borrower | Standard Annual Certification |
| Living Trust Certification, with a surviving borrower | Standard Annual Certification |
| Non-Borrowing Spouse Household Certification | Deferral Period Certification, once the loan has entered its deferral period |

*No longer in force:* the clause stating that on such a move the open cycle's due date is unchanged is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis for the due date a reclassified profile carries.

## Closing

When the last borrower dies and no deferral applies, or when the loan is paid in full, claim-terminated or rescinded as the plan's loan-termination setting provides, the profile closes on the date of death or on the loan's terminated date.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical households)

- A Joint Borrower Certification profile with two borrowers, one of whom dies with an accepted death notice on file for the profile while the loan continues: the profile moves to Standard Annual Certification.
- A Non-Borrowing Spouse Household Certification profile whose only borrower dies: the move to Deferral Period Certification is made once the loan has entered its deferral period.
- A report of death that exists only as a telephone call, with no accepted death notice on file for the profile, supports neither a reclassification nor a closing for the death.

superseded_clauses: the open cycle's due date is unchanged.
